rows.label: 后缀 (-面)

lesson.title: 后缀 -面: 上面 下面 前面 后面 里面 外面
lesson.summary: -面 attaches to position words to make a side or place word: 上面, 下面, 里面.
pattern: 上 / 下 / 前 / 后 / 里 / 外 + 面
body: 面 (miàn) is a suffix that makes a side or place word: 上面 (above), 下面 (below), 前面 (in front), 后面 (behind), 里面 (inside), 外面 (outside). With 在 it names where something is: 书在桌子上面.

The contrast example uses 边, which makes place words the same way (门边, 桌子上边). 边 and 面 are different words; learn each place word as a whole and do not mix them, so 旁边 not 旁面, and 桌子上面 or 桌子上边 rather than a blend.

examples.translation: The book is on the table.

examples.reading: xuéxiào hòumian yǒu yí ge gōngyuán.
examples.translation: There is a park behind the school.
The cat is by the door.

rows.label: 方位名词 (左, 右)

lesson.title: 左 and 右: 左边 右边
lesson.summary: 左 and 右 name sides; add 边 to make 左边 and 右边.
pattern: 在 + noun + 左边 / 右边
body: 左 (zuǒ, left) and 右 (yòu, right) name sides. With a noun they make a place phrase: 桌子左边 (to the left of the table), 学校右边; add 边 to make 左边 / 右边, which can also stand alone: 往左看 (look left), 你的右边.
The contrast example uses 往, which introduces a direction you move toward (往右转), while 左边 / 右边 name a place (在桌子左边). A place word follows 在; a direction word follows 往.

examples.translation: The bank is to the left of the school.

examples.reading: wǒ de jiā zài chāoshì yòubian.
examples.translation: My home is to the right of the supermarket.

rows.label: 动词重叠 (AA, A一A, A了A, ABAB)

lesson.title: Reduplicated verbs: 看看 问一问 看了看
lesson.summary: Repeat a verb to say an action is brief or casual: 看看, 试一试, 看了看.
pattern: V + V: 看看, 想想
V + 一 + V: 试一试; V + 了 + V: 看了看
body: Single-syllable verbs can be reduplicated to say do something a little or casually: 看看, 想想, 听听. A一A puts 一 in the middle: 试一试, 问一问. A了A puts 了 in the middle: 看了看, 试了试. Two-syllable verbs repeat the whole word: 学习学习, 讨论讨论. Verbs like 是, 有 and 在 do not reduplicate.
The contrast example uses 一下 after the verb (请看一下). 一下 also makes an action brief, but the verb itself is not repeated: 看一下 is not 看一看.

rows.label: 能愿动词 (可能)

lesson.title: 可能: maybe, possibly
lesson.summary: Put 可能 before the verb to say something is possible.
body: 可能 (kěnéng) says something is possible: 他可能来, 明天可能下雨, 这件事可能很难. It can also start a short answer: 可能. Negate with 不可能 (impossible); do not say 不可 here.
The contrast example uses 会, which says a skill or a future fact rather than doubt: 他会说汉语. 可能 tells the listener the speaker is not sure.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì kěnéng hěn nán.

rows.label: 离合词 (帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞, 跑步)

lesson.title: 离合词: 帮忙 游泳 跳舞 跑步
lesson.summary: These verbs contain their object; put 了, 个 or a duration between the two parts.
pattern: 帮 + 忙: 帮个忙, 请他帮忙
游 + 泳 / 跳 + 舞: 游了一个小时泳
跑 + 步: 跑了一会儿步
body: 帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞 and 跑步 are separable: 帮+忙, 游+泳, 跳+舞, 跑+步. Put 了, 个 or a duration between the parts: 帮个忙, 我请他帮忙, 游了一个小时泳, 跳了一支舞, 跑了一会儿步. Do not put another object after the whole verb: 帮忙朋友 is wrong.
The contrast example uses the plain verb 帮, which takes a person as its object: 妈妈帮我. 帮忙 is a separable unit, so you say 帮我一个忙, not 帮忙我.

examples.reading: tā yóu le yí ge xiǎoshí yǒng.
tā tiào le yì zhī wǔ.

rows.label: 疑问代词 (为什么)

lesson.title: 为什么: why
lesson.summary: 为什么 asks for a reason; answer with 因为.
body: 为什么 (wèishénme, why) asks for a reason: 你为什么迟到？ 他为什么不来？ Do not add 吗 after it: 你为什么不来吗？ is wrong.
The contrast example answers with 因为: 因为天气不好. 为什么 asks, 因为 answers; the answer to 为什么 is usually a reason clause, not a thing.

examples.translation: Why do you not drink tea?

rows.label: 人称代词 (自己)

lesson.title: 自己: self, by oneself
lesson.summary: A pronoun plus 自己 stresses that person: 我自己, 你自己.
body: 自己 (zìjǐ) follows a pronoun or a name to stress that person: 我自己, 你自己, 他自己. It can stand alone as the subject: 自己的事情自己做. When the subject and object are the same person, use 自己: 他喜欢自己看书.
The contrast example uses 我们 without 自己. A pronoun alone is the plain subject; adding 自己 stresses that these people do it themselves, not someone else.

examples.translation: I go to school by myself.

examples.reading: nǐ zìjǐ zuò fàn, hǎo ma?

rows.label: 指示代词 (那么, 那样, 这么, 这样, 每)

lesson.title: 这么 那么 这样 那样 每
lesson.summary: 这么/那么 show degree; 这样/那样 show manner; 每 means every.
pattern: 这么 / 那么 + adjective / verb
body: 这么 (zhème, so) and 那么 (nàme, so) go before an adjective or a verb to show degree: 这么大, 那么好, 那么喜欢. 这样 (like this) and 那样 (like that) describe manner: 这样做, 那样想. 每 (měi, every) goes with a measure word: 每天, 每个.
The contrast example uses 很, a plain degree adverb: 今天很冷. 这么 and 那么 say so much, often pointing at something or matching a comparison; 很 just gives the degree without that reference.

examples.translation: Let us do it like this.

rows.label: 形容词重叠 (AA, AABB)

lesson.title: Reduplicated adjectives: 大大的 高高兴兴
lesson.summary: Double an adjective for a vivid, warm tone: AA的 or AABB的.
pattern: AA + 的: 大大的, 红红的
AABB + 的: 干干净净的
AABB + 地 + verb: 高高兴兴地
body: Single-syllable adjectives can double to AA, usually with 的: 高高的, 大大的, 红红的. Two-syllable adjectives often become AABB: 高高兴兴, 干干净净, 清清楚楚. A reduplicated adjective goes before the noun with 的 (大大的眼睛) or before the verb with 地 (高高兴兴地回家).
The contrast example uses 很: 这件衣服很漂亮. 很 states a degree; reduplication paints a picture and sounds warmer or more casual. Say 很漂亮, not 很漂漂亮亮.

examples.reading: wǒmen gāogāo xìngxìng de huí jiā.

rows.label: 数词 (万, 好多, 多)

lesson.title: Numbers: 万 好多 多
lesson.summary: 万 is ten thousand; 好多 means a lot; 多 with a noun means many.
body: 万 (wàn) is ten thousand: 一万, 三万; after a number it acts as the unit. 好多 (hǎoduō) means a lot of: 好多书, 好多学生. 多 (duō) before a noun means many: 很多人; in questions it becomes 多少: 多少人.
The contrast example uses 几, which asks for a small approximate number and needs a measure word: 几个朋友. 多少 asks for any amount; 几 expects a small one.

examples.text: 我们学校有一万个学生。
examples.reading: wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu yí wàn ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: Our school has ten thousand students.
There are lots of people in the park.
How many students are there in your class?
How many friends do you have?

rows.label: 名量词 (条, 位, 间, 名; 借用 包)

lesson.title: Measure words: 条 位 间 名 包
lesson.summary: 条 for long things, 位 politely for people, 间 for rooms, 名 for roles, 包 for bags.
pattern: numeral + 条 / 位 / 间 / 名 / 包 + noun
body: 条 (tiáo) counts long, thin things: 一条鱼, 一条路, 一条裤子. 位 (wèi) counts people politely: 一位老师, 两位朋友. 间 (jiān) counts rooms: 一间教室, 两间卧室. 名 (míng) counts people in roles: 一名学生, 两名医生. 包 (bāo) is borrowed from the bag: 一包饼干.
The contrast example uses 个, the general measure from Level 1: 一个书包. Use a specific measure when the noun calls for one, and keep the pair noun and measure together.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le yì tiáo yú.

rows.label: 动量词 (次)

lesson.title: 次: times, occasions
lesson.summary: 次 counts how many times: 一次, 两次, 三次.
body: 次 (cì) counts occasions: 一次 (once), 两次 (twice), 三次 (three times). Put the number and 次 after the verb: 去了一次北京, 看了两次电影. With 过 it counts past experiences: 我去过两次北京. It does not count how long; use a duration such as 一个小时 for that.
The contrast example uses 一下: 我看了一下表. 一下 makes an action brief and is not counted; 次 counts the number of times.

examples.reading: wǒ qù guo yí cì Běijīng.
examples.translation: I have been to Beijing once.

examples.reading: tā kàn le liǎng cì zhè bù diànyǐng.
wǒmen jiàn guo yí cì miàn.
wǒ kàn le yí xià biǎo.
examples.translation: I took a look at my watch.

rows.label: 程度副词 (多, 好, 最)

lesson.title: 多 好 最: exclamation and superlative
lesson.summary: 多 and 好 exclaim before an adjective; 最 picks the highest degree.
body: 多 (duō) before an adjective makes an exclamation: 多甜啊, 多美！ 好 (hǎo) in exclamations means very: 好冷啊, 好漂亮！ 最 (zuì, most) makes the superlative: 最好, 最多, 他最高. Do not put 很 before 最.
The contrast example uses 很: 今天很热. 很 states a degree without exclaiming; 多 and 好 carry feeling, and 最 compares one thing with all others.

examples.reading: tā shì wǒmen bān zuì gāo de.
examples.translation: He is the tallest in our class.

rows.label: 范围副词 (一起)

lesson.title: 一起: together
lesson.summary: 一起 goes after the subject and before the verb to say people do something together.
pattern: A 和 B + 一起 + verb
body: 一起 (yìqǐ, together) stands after the subject and before the verb: 我们一起吃早饭. With two people, join them with 和: 我和爸爸一起看电视. It is an adverb, so it does not stand at the end of the sentence.
The contrast example uses 和 alone: 我和妹妹一起回家. 和 joins two people into one subject; 一起 says they act together. In 我和妹妹一起回家 both are present, and the order of 我 and 妹妹 can be swapped.

examples.reading: wǒ hé bàba yìqǐ kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: Dad and I watch television together.
The classmates go to the library together.

examples.reading: wǒ hé mèimei yìqǐ huí jiā.
examples.translation: My sister and I go home together.

rows.label: 时间副词 (还, 已经, 有时(候), 快, 快要, 正)

lesson.title: Time adverbs: 还 已经 有时 快 正要
lesson.summary: 还 says still; 已经 says already; 有时 says sometimes; 快/快要 say soon; 正 says just now.
pattern: 有时(候) + clause; 快 / 快要 + … + 了
body: 还 (hái, still) says a situation continues: 他还在睡觉. 已经 (yǐjīng, already): 我已经做完作业了. 有时 / 有时候 says occasionally: 我有时候去公园. 快 and 快要 say something is about to happen, usually with 了: 天快下雨了, 快要过年了. 正 stresses the exact moment: 他正看书呢.
The contrast example uses 现在, a time noun: 他现在在看书. 现在 says when; 在 / 正在 / 正 are adverbs placed before the verb. Both 现在我在看书 and 我现在在看书 are possible orders.

examples.reading: wǒ yǐjīng zuò wán zuòyè le.
examples.translation: I have already finished my homework.
I sometimes go to the park.

rows.label: 频率副词 (常, 经常)

lesson.title: 常 and 经常: often
lesson.summary: 常常 and 经常 before the verb mean often; 常 is the short written form.
pattern: subject + 常常 / 经常 + verb
body: 常常 (chángcháng) and 经常 (jīngcháng) mean often and stand before the verb: 我经常去图书馆, 他常常迟到. 常 is the short written form: 常来, 常去. Both describe a habit, not a single occasion.
The contrast example uses 有时: 我有时去公园. 经常 / 常常 mean often or regularly; 有时 means sometimes, so the frequency is lower.

examples.translation: I often go to the library.
Grandfather often goes to the park.
I sometimes go to the park.

rows.label: 否定副词 (别)

lesson.title: 别: do not, don't
lesson.summary: 别 before a verb makes a negative command: 别说话.
body: 别 (bié) is the spoken negative command: 别说, 别走, 别忘了. It tells someone not to do something now or later. It cannot negate the past; say 昨天我没去, not 昨天别去.
The contrast example uses 不要: 请不要在这里抽烟. 别 and 不要 both make negative commands; 别 is shorter and more spoken, 不要 is fuller and common in notices and writing.

examples.translation: Do not forget to bring the book.

examples.reading: qǐng búyào zài zhèlǐ chōu yān.

rows.label: 关联副词 (再, 就)

lesson.title: 再 and 就 linking actions
lesson.summary: 再 says then / next after something else; 就 says then / as early as.
body: 再 as a connective says then after something else: 我先喝水，再吃饭. 就 says an action follows soon or early: 他一来我就走; 我五点就起床. Both link two clauses.
The contrast example uses 才: 他十点才起床. 就 says early or quick; 才 says late or not until, so 就五点 and 才十点 point in opposite directions.

examples.reading: wǒ xiān hē shuǐ, zài chī fàn.
examples.translation: I will drink some water first, then eat.

examples.reading: tā yì lái wǒ jiù zǒu.
examples.translation: As soon as he comes, I will leave.

examples.reading: wǒ wǔ diǎn jiù qǐ chuáng.
examples.translation: I get up as early as five.

examples.reading: tā shí diǎn cái qǐ chuáng.
examples.translation: He did not get up until ten.

rows.label: 语气副词 (都, 就, 还是)

lesson.title: 都 就 还是: attitude words
lesson.summary: 都 stresses even; 就 stresses exactly or just; 还是 suggests or says still.
body: 都 adds emphasis, often with 了: 他都十二岁了. 就 narrows or fixes: 我就想去公园 (that is all I want), 他就十块钱 (exactly ten kuai). 还是 suggests or says something remains: 还是你先去吧, 他还是在睡觉.
The contrast example uses 也: 他也很想去. 都 sums up or stresses even; 也 adds one more. With a singular subject 都 is wrong (say 他也想去, not 他都很想去).

examples.translation: I just want to go to the park.

rows.label: 介词: 引出时间、处所 (从)

lesson.title: 从: from (time and place)
lesson.summary: 从 marks the start of a time or place span; 到 marks the end.
body: 从 (cóng) marks a starting point in space or time: 我从中国来, 从早上到晚上, 从家到学校. It is often paired with 到: 从一楼到三楼. For a pure location use 在, not 从.
The contrast example uses 在: 书在桌子上. 从 introduces where something starts or comes from; 在 says where it is.

examples.reading: cóng zǎoshang dào wǎnshang, tā gōngzuò.
examples.translation: He works from morning till night.

examples.reading: cóng jiā dào xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.translation: It is very close from home to school.
The book is on the table.

rows.label: 介词: 引出方向、路径 (往, 从)

lesson.title: 往 and 从: direction and route
lesson.summary: 往 says toward; 从 says by way of / through.
body: 往 (wǎng) says toward a direction: 往前走, 往左看, 往回走. 从 (cóng) here says by way of or through: 从这条路走, 从桥上过去. 往 is the direction you face or head; 从 is the route taken.
The contrast example uses 到: 我们到学校了. 往 points in a direction; 到 names the place you arrive at.

examples.reading: wǒmen cóng zhè tiáo lù zǒu.

rows.label: 介词: 引出对象 (给, 比, 跟)

lesson.title: 给 比 跟: objects
lesson.summary: 给 introduces the receiver; 比 compares; 跟 introduces the person you act with.
body: 给 (gěi) introduces the receiver: 给他一本书, 给妈妈打电话. 比 (bǐ) compares: 他比我高, 我比弟弟大. 跟 (gēn) introduces the person you do something with: 跟我来, 跟他说话.
The contrast example uses 对: 爸爸对我很好. 跟 says together or with; 对 says an attitude or action is directed toward someone, and it does not take a following verb phrase the same way.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi tā yì běn shū.

examples.translation: Dad is very kind to me.

rows.label: 介词: 引出原因 (因为)

lesson.title: 因为: because
lesson.summary: 因为 introduces a reason; often paired with 所以.
body: 因为 (yīnwèi) introduces a reason clause: 因为下雨, 因为我不舒服. It can answer a question alone: 为什么不来？因为下雨. Often it pairs with 所以 (therefore): 因为下雨，所以我不去.
The contrast example uses 所以: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少. 因为 gives the reason, 所以 gives the result; do not reverse them.

examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒ méiyǒu qù.
examples.translation: Because it rained, I did not go.

examples.reading: yīnwèi shēngbìng, tā méi lái shàngkè.
examples.translation: Because he was ill, he did not come to class.

examples.text: 因为冷，我穿了很多衣服。
examples.reading: yīnwèi lěng, wǒ chuān le hěnduō yīfu.
examples.translation: Because it was cold, I put on many clothes.

examples.text: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià xuě, suǒyǐ lù shang rén hěn shǎo.
examples.translation: Because it snowed, there were few people on the road.

rows.label: 连词: 连接词或短语 (跟)

lesson.title: 跟 joining words: A 跟 B
lesson.summary: 跟 connects two nouns as a compound subject or object, like 和.
body: 跟 (gēn) can join two nouns like 和: 老师跟学生一起去, 我跟你. It is more spoken and northern; 和 is the general form. Do not use 跟 to join clauses; use punctuation or a clause conjunction such as 但是.
The contrast example uses 和: 我喜欢苹果和梨. 和 is neutral and works anywhere; 跟 as a conjunction is informal and joins nouns or pronouns, not whole clauses.

examples.text: 老师跟学生一起去公园。
examples.reading: lǎoshī gēn xuéshēng yìqǐ qù gōngyuán.
examples.translation: The teacher and the students go to the park together.
I will go together with you.

examples.text: 哥哥跟弟弟都喜欢踢足球。
examples.reading: gēge gēn dìdi dōu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.translation: Both the older and the younger brother like playing football.

rows.label: 连词: 连接分句或句子 (但, 但是, 那, 虽然, 还是, 因为, 所以)

lesson.title: Clause conjunctions: 但是 那 虽然 还是
lesson.summary: 这些连词连接分句：但是转折，那承接，虽然/还是让步。
body: 但 and 但是 turn to a contrasting second clause: 我很喜欢这本书，但是太贵了. 那 carries on: 那你就别去了. 虽然 concedes: 虽然下雨，我还是去; 还是 after 虽然 says still. 因为 and 所以 join cause and result: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少.
The contrast example uses 那 as a demonstrative: 那个人是我的老师. 那 before a noun points at something (Level 1); 那 between clauses is the conjunction. The two 那 have the same shape but different jobs.

examples.text: 我很喜欢这本书，但是太贵了。
examples.reading: wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhè běn shū, dànshì tài guì le.
examples.translation: I like this book a lot, but it is too expensive.

examples.reading: nà nǐ jiù bié qù le.

examples.text: 虽然下雨，我们还是去了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ, wǒmen háishì qù le.
examples.translation: Although it rained, we still went.

examples.reading: nàge rén shì wǒ de lǎoshī.

rows.label: 结构助词 (得, 地)

lesson.title: 得 and 地: complement and adverbial markers
lesson.summary: 得 after a verb introduces a complement; 地 after an adjective marks how an action is done.
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of the action: 说得很好, 跑得很快. 地 (de) after an adjective or adverb modifies the verb: 慢慢地走, 高兴地说. Both are read neutral in these positions.
The contrast example uses 的: 这是我的书. 的 before a noun marks possession or attribution; 得 follows a verb; 地 comes before a verb it modifies. The same sound has three different jobs.

rows.label: 动态助词 (过)

lesson.title: 过: past experience
lesson.summary: Verb + 过 says the action has happened at least once; negate with 没(有)…过.
body: 过 (guo) after a verb marks an experience in the past: 我去过中国, 你吃过烤鸭吗. To say it never happened, put 没(有) before the verb and keep 过 after it: 我没去过上海. Do not use 不 here.
The contrast example uses 了: 我吃了两个苹果. 过 says the speaker has had the experience at some time; 了 says the action was completed on that occasion.

examples.reading: nǐ chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā ma?
examples.translation: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?
I have never been to Shanghai.

examples.reading: wǒ chī le liǎng ge píngguǒ.

rows.label: 动态助词 (着)

lesson.title: 着: continuing state
lesson.summary: Verb + 着 says a state holds or a posture continues: 门开着, 他拿着一本书.
body: 着 (zhe) after a verb marks a continuing state or posture: 门开着, 他穿着一件白衬衫, 他拿着一本书. It often describes a scene or background: 墙上挂着一幅画 (see 存现句).
The contrast example uses 在: 他在看书. 着 describes a state that holds; 在 / 正在 describe an action happening now. 门开着 is a state, 门在开 is an action in progress.

examples.reading: tā ná zhe yì běn shū.
tā chuān zhe yí jiàn bái chènshān.
examples.translation: She is wearing a white shirt.

rows.label: 语气助词 (呢, 吧, 的, 啊)

lesson.title: 呢 吧 的 啊: sentence-final particles
lesson.summary: 呢 asks or marks ongoing; 吧 suggests; 的 confirms; 啊 exclaims or softens.
body: 呢 (ne) asks a follow-up question or marks an ongoing state: 你呢？, 他吃饭呢. 吧 (ba) softens a suggestion or guess: 我们走吧, 是吧. 的 (de) confirms: 他会来的. 啊 (a) exclaims or softens: 真好啊, 快来啊.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你是学生吗？ 吗 makes a plain yes-no question; 呢 / 吧 / 的 / 啊 each color the sentence differently and cannot replace 吗 there.

rows.label: 短语: 基本结构类型 (动补短语1)

lesson.title: Verb-complement phrases: V + result/degree
lesson.summary: A complement follows the verb and adds its result or degree: 看见, 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + complement: 看 + 见, 做 + 完
body: In a verb-complement phrase the second part tells what happens to the action: 看见 (see and perceive), 听懂 (listen and understand), 做完 (finish doing), 看清楚. It is different from a verb-object phrase, where the second part is the thing acted on: 看书, 吃饭.
The contrast example uses a verb-object phrase: 我吃饭. 吃饭 takes a thing (the object); 做完 takes a result (the complement).

rows.label: 短语: 其他结构类型 (的字短语, 连谓短语, 兼语短语)

lesson.title: Phrases: …的, serial verbs, pivotal phrases
lesson.summary: 的字短语 stands for a thing; 连谓短语 chains verbs; 兼语短语 shares one person between verbs.
pattern: 请/让 + person + V (兼语短语)
body: 的字短语: 的 after a phrase stands for a thing or person: 我的, 红色的, 卖菜的. 连谓短语: two verbs share one subject and happen together or in order: 去买菜, 笑着说. 兼语短语: the object of the first verb is also the subject of the second: 请他来, 让我走.
The contrast example uses 和: 我有哥哥和姐姐. 和 joins two nouns into one phrase; it does not chain verbs or make a pivotal structure.

examples.translation: I have an older brother and an older sister.

rows.label: 短语: 功能类型 (名词性, 动词性, 形容词性)

lesson.title: Phrase functions: noun, verb, adjective
lesson.summary: A phrase can act as a noun, a verb or an adjective: 新书, 去买菜, 很大.
pattern: 名词性: 新的书 / 我的书
动词性: 去买菜 / 喜欢看书
形容词性: 很大 / 红红的
body: By function, a phrase can behave like a noun (名词性: 一本新书, 我的书), like a verb (动词性: 去买菜, 喜欢看书), or like an adjective (形容词性: 很大, 干干净净的). Function depends on the head word and on where the phrase sits in the sentence.
The contrast example uses 的: 我的书在桌子上. 的 turns pronoun plus noun into a noun phrase; without 的 you cannot put those two words together as one modifier.

examples.reading: zhè shì yì běn xīn shū.
wǒ de shū zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.translation: My book is on the table.

rows.label: 固定短语 (什么的)

lesson.title: 什么的: and so on
lesson.summary: 什么的 follows a list to mean and so on: 苹果、香蕉什么的.
body: 什么的 (shénme de) follows one or more items to mean and so on: 我喜欢吃苹果、香蕉什么的; 他买了书、本子什么的. It is informal. Do not use 什么的 when only one item is named, and do not mix it with 等.
The contrast example uses 和: 我喜欢苹果和梨. 和 links exactly two items; 什么的 closes a list of two or more and adds and so on.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le shū, běnzi shénme de.
examples.translation: He bought books, notebooks and so on.

examples.text: 我喜欢唱歌、跳舞什么的。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan chànggē, tiàowǔ shénme de.
examples.translation: I like singing, dancing and so on.

examples.text: 周末我常看书、运动什么的。
examples.reading: zhōumò wǒ cháng kàn shū, yùndòng shénme de.
examples.translation: At weekends I often read, exercise and so on.

rows.label: 固定格式 (还是……吧)

lesson.title: 还是……吧: a gentle suggestion
lesson.summary: 还是……吧 suggests an option after thinking it over: 我们还是走吧.
body: 还是……吧 makes a gentle suggestion or a choice after weighing things: 我们还是坐出租车去吧, 你还是先吃饭吧. It softens advice; 吧 alone can also suggest, but 还是…吧 adds an afterthought.
The contrast example uses 好吗: 我们明天去，好吗？ 好吗 asks whether the listener agrees; 还是…吧 recommends one option instead of asking.

examples.reading: nǐ háishì xiān chī fàn ba.
wǒmen háishì zuò dìtiě qù ba.
examples.translation: We had better go by underground.

rows.label: 固定格式 (要/快要/就要……了)

lesson.title: 要……了: about to happen
lesson.summary: 要/快要/就要…了 says something is just going to happen.
pattern: 快要 / 就要 + V + 了
body: 要…了, 快要…了 and 就要…了 all say an event is about to happen: 要下雨了, 火车快要到了, 他就要回来了. Add 了 at the end. 快要 is one word; 就要 stresses that the time is right.
The contrast example uses 已经: 他已经回家了. 已经 says the event already happened; 要 / 快要 say it has not happened yet.

examples.translation: He is about to come back.

rows.label: 固定格式 (都……了)

lesson.title: 都……了: lateness or amount
lesson.summary: 都……了 stresses that something is later or larger than expected.
body: 都……了 stresses surprise or lateness: 都十点了，快睡吧; 他都十八岁了; 都三点了，他还没来. It sums up the scale and adds 了. This is not the 都 that sums people before the verb (我们都去).
The contrast example uses 已经: 我已经吃过了. 已经 simply says already; 都…了 adds surprise that it is so late or so much.

examples.reading: dōu shí diǎn le, kuài shuì ba.
examples.translation: It is already ten o'clock; go to sleep.

examples.reading: dōu sān diǎn le, tā hái méi lái.
examples.translation: It is already three, and he has not come.

rows.label: 主语 (受事主语)

lesson.title: Patient subjects: the thing comes first
lesson.summary: In a patient-subject sentence the thing receives the action: 作业做完了.
body: In a patient-subject sentence the subject is the thing the action happens to: 作业做完了, 苹果吃完了, 这本书我看过了. The doer can be left out because it is known or unimportant. This is not the passive with 被 (Level 3).

The contrast example uses the doer as subject: 我做完了作业. A patient-subject sentence puts the thing first (受事主语); an ordinary sentence puts the doer first (施事主语). Both orders are possible here, so the word-order exercise is skipped.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū wǒ kàn guo le.

rows.label: 谓语 (名词性短语作谓语)

lesson.title: Noun-phrase predicates
lesson.summary: A noun phrase can be the predicate directly: 今天星期三, 他北京人.
body: With dates, weekdays, places and origins, Chinese often drops 是 and puts a noun phrase directly after the subject: 今天星期三, 他北京人, 明天晴天. Adding 是 is possible and more formal: 今天是星期三.

The contrast example uses 是: 他是老师. 是 equates the subject with the noun; the noun-phrase predicate without 是 is used for classification details such as date, origin and weather, and sounds more spoken.

rows.label: 定语 (动词或动词性短语、主谓短语作定语)

lesson.title: Attributives: verb phrases and subject-predicate phrases
lesson.summary: A verb phrase or subject-predicate phrase can modify a noun with 的: 我买的书, 身体好的学生.
body: An attributive (定语) comes before the noun and usually takes 的: 我买的书, 昨天来的客人. A subject-predicate phrase can also be an attributive: 身体好的学生, 天气冷的冬天. Some short attributives drop 的: 汉语老师.
The contrast example uses 地: 他高兴地说. An attributive with 的 goes before a noun; an adverbial with 地 goes before a verb. Check what follows the marker, not just the sound.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi de shū hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: The book I bought is very good.

examples.text: 昨天来的客人是我的老师。
examples.reading: zuótiān lái de kèren shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.translation: The guest who came yesterday is my teacher.

examples.text: 身体好的学生都很努力。
examples.reading: shēntǐ hǎo de xuéshēng dōu hěn nǔlì.
examples.translation: Students in good health all work hard.

rows.label: 结果补语1 (错, 懂, 好, 会, 完)

lesson.title: Result complements: 错 懂 好 会 完
lesson.summary: A result complement after the verb says how the action turns out: 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + 完 / 好 / 懂 / 会 / 错
body: 完 (finish), 好 (done well or ready), 懂 (understand), 会 (know how) and 错 (wrong) follow the verb as results: 写完, 做好, 听懂, 学会, 做错. To say the result did not happen, insert 不: 听不懂, 做不完; with 得 it says possibility: 听得懂, 做得完.
The contrast example uses 得: 他说得很好. A result complement attaches the outcome directly to the verb; 得 introduces a description of manner or degree.

examples.reading: wǒ tīng dǒng lǎoshī de huà le.
examples.translation: I understood what the teacher said.

rows.label: 趋向补语1: 简单趋向 (来, 去, 上, 下, 进, 出, 回, 过, 起)

lesson.title: Simple directional complements
lesson.summary: A one-syllable direction word follows the verb: 寄来, 上楼, 走进.
pattern: V + 进 / 出 / 回 / 过
body: 简单趋向补语 is one syllable after the verb: 来 toward the speaker, 去 away, 上 up or onto, 下 down or off, 进 into, 出 out of, 回 back, 过 across, 起 up. With a thing object, put the complement before the object: 寄来一封信, 拿回来一本书.
The contrast example uses the compound 上来: 他走上来了. A compound has two syllables (上 + 来); a simple complement has one (上 or 来). Learn them as separate words.

examples.reading: tā jì lái yì fēng xìn.

rows.label: 趋向补语1: 复合趋向 (上来, 下来, 进去, 出来, 回来, 过来, 起来)

lesson.title: Compound directional complements
lesson.summary: Two-syllable complements combine directions: 上来, 下来, 进来, 出来, 回来.
pattern: V + 下来 / 下去; V + 起来
V + 进来 / 进去; V + 出来 / 出去; V + 回来 / 过来
body: 复合趋向补语 combines two directions: 上 + 来 = 上来, 下 + 去 = 下去, 进 + 来 = 进来, 出 + 去 = 出去, 回 + 来 = 回来, 过 + 来 = 过来, 起 + 来 = 起来. The second syllable points relative to the speaker: 来 toward, 去 away.
The contrast example uses the simple 上: 他走上楼了. 上 alone is a simple complement; 上来 is its compound form. Both describe movement, but they are different words.

examples.text: 他从楼上拿下来一本书。
examples.reading: tā cóng lóu shàng ná xiàlai yì běn shū.
examples.translation: He brought a book down from upstairs.

rows.label: 状态补语1 (动词+得+形容词性短语)

lesson.title: State complements: V + 得 + adjective
lesson.summary: 得 after a verb describes how the action is done: 说得很好, 跑得很快.
pattern: V + 得 + 很 / 非常 + adj
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of the action: 他说得很好, 妹妹长得很高, 他跑得比我快. This is different from a result complement such as 做完, and from an adverb before the verb such as 很好地.
The contrast example uses the result complement 完: 他说完了. 得 describes manner or degree; a result complement states the outcome directly.

examples.translation: My younger sister has grown very tall.

rows.label: 数量补语2 (时量补语; 形容词+数量补语)

lesson.title: Quantity complements: duration and measurement
lesson.summary: Duration follows the verb: 住了两年; measurement follows an adjective: 大两岁.
body: Duration (时量补语) follows the verb, often with 了: 我住了一年, 他等了一个小时. An adjective plus a quantity states a difference or size: 他比我大三岁, 这条路长一百米, 这座山有一千米高.
The contrast example uses 次: 我去过两次北京. 次 counts occasions; duration counts how long, and adjective + quantity measures a difference.

examples.reading: wǒ zài Zhōngguó zhù le liǎng nián.
examples.translation: I lived in China for two years.

examples.reading: tā děng le yí ge xiǎoshí.
tā bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.translation: He is three years older than me.

examples.reading: wǒ qù guo liǎng cì Běijīng.
examples.translation: I have been to Beijing twice.

rows.label: 单句 (主谓谓语句)

lesson.title: Subject-predicate predicates
lesson.summary: A whole subject-predicate phrase comments on the topic: 他身体很好.
body: In a 主谓谓语句 the predicate itself is a subject-predicate phrase: 他身体很好 (topic 他, comment 身体很好), 这件事我不清楚. The first noun is the topic, and the following subject belongs to it.
The contrast example uses an ordinary verb-plus-object sentence: 我喜欢汉语. A subject-predicate predicate comments on a topic; an ordinary sentence states an action with an object.

examples.translation: He is in very good health.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì wǒ bù qīngchu.
examples.translation: I am not clear about this matter.

rows.label: 疑问句 (还是选择问句)

lesson.title: 还是 choice questions
lesson.summary: A还是B? asks the listener to choose one of two options.
body: 还是 makes an alternative question: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？ 今天还是明天？ The answer is one of the two, not yes or no. Do not add 吗 to the sentence.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你想喝茶吗？ 吗 makes a yes-no question; 还是 offers two choices. Choose the particle that matches the answer you expect.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishì kāfēi?
examples.translation: Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.reading: nǐ zuò huǒchē háishì zuò fēijī?
examples.translation: Will you take the train or the plane?

rows.label: 祈使句 (别)

lesson.title: Imperative sentences with 别
lesson.summary: Commands start with a verb or 请; 别… tells someone not to do it.
body: An imperative drops the subject and starts with the verb, often with 请 (please) or 别 (do not): 请坐, 请喝茶, 别说话. 别 is direct and spoken.
The contrast example uses 不要: 请不要在教室里跑. 别 and 不要 both command someone not to act; 不要 is fuller and more formal, while 别 is short and colloquial.

examples.reading: qǐng búyào zài jiàoshì li pǎo.
examples.translation: Please do not run in the classroom.

rows.label: “是”字句2 (解释或说明)

lesson.title: 是 for explanation and characteristics
lesson.summary: 是 plus a quality or category explains what something is like: 这个苹果是甜的.
body: 是 can explain a characteristic or category, often with 的 at the end: 这个苹果是甜的, 这件衣服是毛的, 他是教书的. It states a fact about the subject rather than an action.
The contrast example uses 很: 这个苹果很甜. 很 describes the degree; 是…的 affirms the quality as a fact or classification. They are close in meaning but not interchangeable in structure.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu shì máo de.
examples.translation: This garment is made of wool.
He is a teacher by profession.

rows.label: “有”字句2 (达到一个数量)

lesson.title: 有 + quantity: reaching a measure
lesson.summary: 有 plus a quantity says how deep, long or high something is.
body: 有 with a quantity states an extent or measurement: 这条河有十米深, 这条路有二十公里长, 这座山有一千米高. It says the thing reaches that measure.
The contrast example uses 很: 这条河很深. 很 only says the degree (very deep); 有 + quantity gives a measured amount.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo hé yǒu shí mǐ shēn.
examples.translation: This river is ten metres deep.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo lù yǒu èrshí gōnglǐ cháng.
examples.translation: This road is twenty kilometres long.

examples.reading: zhè zuò shān yǒu yì qiān mǐ gāo.
examples.translation: This mountain is one thousand metres high.

rows.label: 存现句2 (地方+动词+着+数量+名词)

lesson.title: Existential sentences: place + verb + 着 + noun
lesson.summary: A place plus a verb with 着 says something is there: 桌子上放着一本书.
body: Place words start the sentence, then a verb with 着, then the thing: 桌子上放着一本书, 墙上挂着一幅画, 门口站着一个人. 着 marks a state, and the thing after it is indefinite, so use 一本 / 一个, not 这 / 那.
The contrast example uses 在: 我在看书. An existential sentence describes what is at a place (a state); 在 + verb describes an action happening now.

examples.reading: zhuōzi shàng fàng zhe yì běn shū.
examples.translation: There is a book on the table.

examples.reading: qiáng shàng guà zhe yì fú huà.
examples.translation: There is a picture on the wall.

examples.reading: ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí ge rén.
examples.translation: A person is standing at the door.

rows.label: 比较句1 (A比B+形; A有/没有B+形; A比B+V+得+形)

lesson.title: Comparisons: A 比 B …
lesson.summary: 比 compares two things; 没有 says not as … as; with a verb use 得.
pattern: A + 比 + B + adj + 数量; A + 没有 + B + adj
A + 比 + B + V + 得 + adj
body: 比 (bǐ) puts the standard after it: 他比我高, 我比弟弟大两岁. To say A is not as … as B, use 没有: 我没有他高; to say A reaches B, use 有: 他有我这么高. With a verb, add 得: 他比我唱得好.
The contrast example uses 一样: 他和我一样高. 比 shows a difference; 一样 says the two are equal.

examples.reading: wǒ bǐ dìdi dà liǎng suì.
examples.translation: I am two years older than my brother.
He is not as tall as me.
He is as tall as me.

rows.label: “是……的”句1 (强调时间、地点、方式、施事)

lesson.title: 是……的: emphasizing details of an event
lesson.summary: 是……的 stresses when, where, how or who did something: 我是昨天到的.
body: 是……的 emphasizes a detail of an event, usually in the past: 我是昨天到的, 他是坐火车来的, 我是在书店买的. The 是 can be dropped; the 的 stays. Use it to answer when / where / how questions about the event.
The contrast example uses 了: 我昨天去了北京. 是……的 emphasizes the detail; 了 simply says the action was completed. Both are possible orders with 昨天, so the word-order exercise is skipped for that example.

examples.reading: tā shì zuò huǒchē lái de.
wǒ shì zài shūdiàn mǎi de.
examples.translation: I bought it at the bookshop.

rows.label: 兼语句1 (请/叫/让+对象1+动词+对象2)

lesson.title: Pivotal sentences: 请 叫 让 someone do something
lesson.summary: 请/叫/让 take a person, and that person does the next verb: 请他来, 让我走.
body: In a pivotal sentence the object of 请 / 叫 / 让 is also the subject of the next verb: 老师请我们回答问题, 妈妈叫我早点睡, 他让我先走. Do not add 是 or 的 between them.
The contrast example uses 和: 我和朋友一起去. 和 joins two people who do one action together; 请 / 叫 / 让 introduce a person who then performs a second action.

examples.translation: The teacher asked us to answer the question.
Mum told me to go to bed early.
I will go together with a friend.

rows.label: 双宾语句2 (主语+动词+给+对象1+对象2)

lesson.title: Double objects with 给: send someone something
lesson.summary: S + V + 给 + person + thing: 他寄给我一个包裹.
body: With verbs such as 送, 寄 and 告诉, put 给 before the person: 他送给我一本书, 他寄给我一个包裹, 老师发给我们一张纸. The thing follows the person; 给 marks the receiver.
The contrast example uses 把: 他把书给我. The 把 construction moves the thing before the verb; the 给 double-object sentence keeps person and thing after the verb.

examples.reading: tā jì gěi wǒ yí ge bāoguǒ.
māma jì gěi wǒ yì fēng xìn.
tā sòng gěi wǒ yì zhāng piào.

examples.translation: He gave the book to me.

rows.label: 选择复句 ((是)……, 还是……)

lesson.title: Alternative complex sentences: 是……，还是……
lesson.summary: (是) A，还是 B offers two clauses as choices.
body: (是)……，还是…… joins two clauses as choices: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？ 我们是今天走，还是明天走？ It is the sentence form of the A还是B? question, and the answer is one clause.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你明天走吗？ 吗 asks for yes or no; 是…还是… asks the listener to pick one of two clauses.

examples.text: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？
examples.reading: nǐ shì zài jiā kàn shū, háishì qù túshūguǎn?
examples.translation: Will you read at home, or go to the library?

examples.text: 我们是今天走，还是明天走？
examples.reading: wǒmen shì jīntiān zǒu, háishì míngtiān zǒu?
examples.translation: Shall we leave today, or tomorrow?

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng chī mǐfàn, háishì miàntiáo?
examples.translation: Would you like rice, or noodles?

rows.label: 转折复句 (虽然……, 但是……)

lesson.title: Concessive sentences: 虽然……，但是……
lesson.summary: 虽然 admits a fact, 但是 turns to the opposite result.
body: 虽然 (suīrán) concedes something; 但是 turns to the unexpected: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好; 虽然下雨，我们还是去了. The two clauses often contrast, and 但是 belongs in the second clause.
The contrast example uses 因为…所以…: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了. 虽然…但是… links concession and turn; 因为…所以… links cause and result.

examples.text: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好。
examples.reading: suīrán hěn guì, dànshì zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: It is expensive, but the quality is good.

examples.text: 虽然下雨，我们还是去了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ, wǒmen háishì qù le.
examples.translation: Although it rained, we still went.

examples.text: 虽然他很累，但是他还在工作。
examples.reading: suīrán tā hěn lèi, dànshì tā hái zài gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Although he is tired, he is still working.

examples.text: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
examples.translation: Because it rained, the match was cancelled.

rows.label: 因果复句 (因为……, 所以……)

lesson.title: Cause and result: 因为……，所以……
lesson.summary: 因为 gives the reason, 所以 the result.
body: 因为…所以… links a reason and its result: 因为生病，所以他没来; 因为下雪，路上车很少. 因为 can stand alone in an answer, and 所以 usually introduces the second clause.
The contrast example uses 虽然…但是…: 虽然下雨，但是我还是去了. A causal sentence says one thing caused another; a concessive sentence admits a fact and turns against it.

examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bú qù.
examples.translation: Because it is raining, I am not going.

examples.reading: yīnwèi shēngbìng, tā méi lái shàngkè.
examples.translation: Because he was ill, he did not come to class.

examples.text: 因为下雪，所以路上车很少。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià xuě, suǒyǐ lù shang chē hěn shǎo.
examples.translation: Because it snowed, there were few cars on the road.

examples.text: 虽然下雨，但是我还是去了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ, dànshì wǒ háishì qù le.
examples.translation: Although it rained, I still went.

rows.label: 紧缩复句 (一……就……)

lesson.title: 一……就……: as soon as
lesson.summary: 一……就… links two immediate actions: 我一放学就回家。
body: 一……就…… says the second action follows the first immediately: 他一回来就给我打电话; 天一冷就下雪. The two clauses share the subject, and 就 stands in the second.
The contrast example uses 先……再……: 我先吃饭，再去散步. 一…就… stresses that there is no gap; 先…再… only lists steps in order.

examples.reading: wǒ yí fàngxué jiù huí jiā.
examples.translation: As soon as school finishes, I go home.

examples.text: 他一回来就给我打电话。
examples.reading: tā yì huílai jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.translation: As soon as he gets back, he will call me.

examples.reading: tiān yì lěng jiù xià xuě.
examples.translation: As soon as it turns cold, it snows.

examples.reading: wǒ xiān chī fàn, zài qù sàn bù.
examples.translation: I will eat first, then go for a walk.

rows.label: 持续态 (动词+着)

lesson.title: 持续态: verb + 着
lesson.summary: 着 after a verb says a state continues or an action keeps going.
body: 着 marks a continuing state or action: 门开着, 他坐着看书, 树上挂着很多苹果. It often describes how things are, especially a background scene. Compare the progressive 在, which says an action is happening now.
The contrast example uses 在: 他在看书. 着 presents a held state or continuation; 在 presents an action in progress at this moment.

examples.reading: shù shàng guà zhe hěnduō píngguǒ.
examples.translation: Many apples are hanging on the tree.
The light is on in the room.

rows.label: 经历态 (过)

lesson.title: 经历态: verb + 过
lesson.summary: 过 says someone has had the experience at least once: 我去过中国。
body: As an aspect, 过 says an action has been experienced, not when it happened: 我去过中国, 他吃过烤鸭. Ask 你吃过…吗？ Negate with 没: 我没去过. It does not combine with a specific past time such as 昨天; use 了 for that.
The contrast example uses 了: 我昨天去了北京. 过 looks back over an indefinite past; 了 anchors the action to the stated occasion.

examples.translation: Have you ever eaten roast duck?
I have never been to Shanghai.

rows.label: 数的表达法 (序数2: 数词+量词)

lesson.title: Number + measure: floors, classes, grades
lesson.summary: A number plus a measure names an ordered item: 二楼, 三班, 五年级.
pattern: numeral + measure (+ noun): 二楼, 三班
numeral + 年级 / 层 / 号
body: To name floors, classes, grades and rooms, put the number directly before the measure word, without 第: 二楼, 三班, 五年级, 四号房间. This is a label for an ordered unit, not a count of things: 三楼 means the third floor, not three floors.
The contrast example uses 第: 我的座位在第五排. 第 + number gives the position in a row or sequence; number + measure names a fixed label such as a floor or a class.

examples.translation: My home is on the third floor.

examples.reading: wǒ de zuòwèi zài dì-wǔ pái.
examples.translation: My seat is in the fifth row.

rows.label: 概数表达法1 (几; 数词+多+量词; 数词+量词+多)

lesson.title: Approximate numbers: 几, 十多, 一年多
lesson.summary: 几 asks a small approximate number; 多 after a number or a measure means more than.
body: 几 (jǐ) asks for a rough small number: 几个人, 几个苹果. 多 after a number means more than: 十多个, 三十多个人. 多 after the measure means more than that many units: 三年多, 五个多月. Do not say 三个多人.
The contrast example uses 多少: 你们班有多少人？ 几 suggests a small amount and needs a measure word; 多少 asks about any amount and goes straight before the noun.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li yǒu shí duō ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: There are more than ten students in the classroom.

examples.reading: tā xué le yì nián duō Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: He has studied Chinese for more than a year.
How many people are there in your class?
